Affected baseline items: 3:chicken, 6:check-in-process, 7:with-small-fries-add-dollar2, 8:100-pieces, 9:crispy-seasoned-shrimp-lettuce-tomato, 13:fettuccine-pasta-tossed-with-our-unique-alfredo-sauce-and-topped-with-parmesan-cheese, 14:fresh-grilled-salmon-served-with-rice-and-vegetables-in-lemon-butter-sauce, 15:fried-corn-tortillas-served-with-our-home-made-traditional-mexican-salsa, 19:seasoned-and-breaded-catfish-w-2-sides, 21:starbuzz, 22:sunday-brunch, 25:200pm, 26:400pm, 27:700pm, 28:starbuzz-7-00pm-close, 29:starbuzz-citrus-mist-love66-new-impressionz-hookah-prices-hookah-sunday-to-thursday-4-00pm-9-00pm, and 30:starbuzz-hookah-friday-to-saturday-2-00pm-4-00pm.

Reconciliation covers 30 of 30 baseline rows and 30 unique rows with no duplicate reconciled keys. Counts are: variant_match/accurately_unavailable 1, variant_match/verified 2, variant_match/mismatch 4, artifact/not_applicable 14, normalized_match/mismatch 6, normalized_match/accurately_unavailable 1, stale_extra/not_applicable 1, and normalized_match/verified 1.

The catalog-underdefinition discrepancy is confirmed. Luna defines 13 current products, while the restaurant-issued food and happy-hour pages enumerate dozens of separately orderable products and variants.
The unresolved-surface risk is confirmed narrowly: the official brunch page is non-enumerable and therefore cannot establish completeness, absences, allergen negatives, or cross-contact conclusions.

The allergen-overclaim discrepancy is confirmed. Unsupported baseline positives include shellfish for CHICKEN; milk for the fries modifier; milk/wheat/gluten for the 100 PIECES fragment; milk for the shrimp-description fragment; wheat/gluten/shellfish for the fettuccine description; shellfish for grilled salmon; milk for chips-and-salsa description; and milk/shellfish for breaded catfish.

Valid explicit positives must remain: shrimp supports shellfish; salmon and catfish support fish; cheese, Parmesan, Alfredo sauce, and butter support milk. These are narrow positive ingredient or unavoidable-identity findings, not complete allergen arrays.
Fettuccine or generic pasta identity alone does not reliably establish wheat or gluten; breaded identity alone does not reliably establish wheat. Those promotions would be culinary assumptions.

No restaurant-issued allergen matrix or cross-contact disclosure was found. The raw/undercooked-food warning is not cross-contact evidence. Empty arrays on incomplete ingredient prose cannot be interpreted as allergen negatives or completeness.

Count drift, current-only omissions, non-exact reconciliation, validation-warning, authority-ambiguity, and scout-risk gates remain materially supported. Duplicate presentation counts reflect real overlapping menu surfaces but are not independently proof of an erroneous product duplication.

Terra's claim that the current shisha page lists Al Fakher instead of Starbuzz is false. The reopened restaurant-issued page explicitly lists both AL FAKHER and STARBUZZ, including Starbuzz flavors and price periods.

Reject terra-shisha-starbuzz-drift and the claim that audit item 21:starbuzz is stale solely because Starbuzz is absent. The related baseline-only and surface-mismatch conclusions require re-reconciliation against the presently visible Starbuzz section.
Reject the additional-product note stating that Luna represented Starbuzz 'instead of' Al Fakher. Both catalogs are currently present.
Reject any complete or negative allergen conclusion derived from the accessible food menu's partial descriptions, including treating empty contains/may-contain arrays as verified absence.
Reject Terra's narrow positive assignment of wheat to fettuccine when supported only by the generic product identity rather than an explicit wheat ingredient.
